facts.fact_text: From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the post-election protest rallies was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
The applicant was actively involved in the post-election protests following the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election.
The applicant regularly attended the demonstrations held at Freedom Square in Yerevan.
The applicant gave speeches at the demonstrations held at Freedom Square in Yerevan.
On 1 March 2008, at some point around 6-7 a.m., a police operation was conducted at Freedom Square in Yerevan where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
The applicant alleged that the aim of the police operation on 1 March 2008 at Freedom Square had been forcibly to terminate the assembly.
The applicant alleged that a large police force had violently attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square with rubber batons and electric shock devices, without any prior warning.
The applicant alleged that the police attack on demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 forced the demonstrators to flee the square.
On 1 March 2008 a criminal case was instituted under several Articles of the Armenian Criminal Code in connection with the events at Freedom Square.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of organising and holding an unlawful assembly.
The criminal case instituted on 1 March 2008 in connection with the events at Freedom Square included charges of incitement to disobedience of police orders to terminate the unlawful assembly.
On 10 March 2008 the applicant was arrested by officers of the National Security Service on suspicion of usurpation of State power.
On 12 March 2008 the applicant was charged under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.
On 12 March 2008 the applicant was charged under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (usurpation of State power) within the scope of criminal case no. 62202608.
On 12 March 2008 a court ordered the applicant's pre-trial detention.
On 22 June 2009 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code of organising mass disorder.
On 22 June 2009 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant to five years in prison.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 presidential election, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan organised and held mass public events at Yerevan's Freedom Square in violation of the procedure prescribed by law.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that members of parliament K.S. and S.M. organised and held mass public events at Yerevan's Freedom Square in violation of the procedure prescribed by law.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that the chief editor of Haykakan Zhamanak daily newspaper, N.P., organised and held mass public events at Yerevan's Freedom Square in violation of the procedure prescribed by law.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that the organisers and participants made calls inciting disobedience of decisions ordering an end to the events held in violation of the procedure prescribed by law.
The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that a number of participants in the mass events illegally possessed and carried illegally obtained arms and ammunition.

The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that on 1 March 2008 at around 6 a.m., when the police took measures aimed at forcibly ending the public events held in violation of the procedure prescribed by law in compliance with the requirements of section 14 of the Assemblies, Rallies, Marches and Demonstrations Act, the organisers and participants committed a life- and health-threatening assault on police officers with clubs, metal rods and other adapted objects.
The decision to institute criminal proceedings on 1 March 2008 stated that the assault on police officers caused the police officers injuries of varied severity.

The decision to institute the criminal case on 2 March 2008 stated that Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan, the candidate running for president at the 19 February 2008 presidential election, and his followers and supporters, including members of parliament K.S. and S.M., the chief editor of Haykakan Zhamanak daily newspaper N.P., and others, not willing to concede defeat at the election, organised mass disorder involving murders, violence, massacre, arson, destruction of property and armed resistance to public officials, with the use of firearms, explosives and other adapted objects, from 1 March 2008 in the area of the Yerevan Mayor's Office and central streets.

The decision to institute the criminal case on 2 March 2008 stated that the aim of the organisers was to cast doubt on the 19 February 2008 presidential election, instil distrust towards the results among large segments of the population, create illusions of public discontent and revolt, and discredit the election and the authorities.

The charging decision of 12 March 2008 stated that after the 19 February 2008 presidential election, the applicant joined the group of supporters of Levon Ter-Petrosyan and, having conspired with them to usurp State power in violation of the constitutional order, actively participated in carrying out activities for that purpose.

The charging decision of 12 March 2008 stated that the applicant's activities included discrediting the pre-election process and the conduct of the election, instilling distrust towards the results among large segments of the population, creating illusions of public discontent and revolt, and organising and holding unlawful demonstrations aimed at destabilising the internal political situation.

The charging decision of 12 March 2008 stated that the applicant, three other members of parliament and a number of other opposition supporters incited and organised mass disorder which took place in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008.

The charging decision of 12 March 2008 stated that the mass disorder in Yerevan on 1 and 2 March 2008 involved mass violence, massacre, arson, destruction and damage of public and private property, armed resistance to public officials and murder.
On 31 March 2009 the prosecutor replaced the charge against the applicant under Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code with a charge under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
On 31 March 2009 the prosecutor dropped the charge against the applicant under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.
The prosecutor dropped the charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code on the ground that on 24 March 2009 Article 225 § 3 of the Armenian Criminal Code had been repealed.

The prosecutor dropped the charge under Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code on the ground that Article 300 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code had been amended and could not be applied retroactively.
On 22 June 2009 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty under Article 225 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code of organising mass disorder.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and S.S., together with a group of people, starting from 20 February 2008 carried out organisational activities for the purpose of creating discontent in society towards the conduct and results of the 19 February 2008 presidential election and preparing the crowd gathered at Freedom Square for use of violence and disobedience.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and S.S. spread false information about the assembly at Freedom Square being authorised by the municipal authorities, about around 500,000 people attending it, about the election result being rigged, and about presidential candidate Levon Ter-Petrosyan winning 60% of the votes cast.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and S.S. provided participants of the assembly at Freedom Square with household items and money in order to ensure the constant presence of people at the assembly.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that rods, clubs, armature, petrol bombs, metal constructions used as missile weapons, firearms and ammunition were distributed to a group of participants of the assembly at Freedom Square.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that on 29 February 2008 intelligence information was received by the Armenian Police and the National Security Service that a group of persons intended to instigate mass disorder in Yerevan on 1 March 2008 through provocations and that a large quantity of clubs, metal rods, explosive substances, firearms and grenades were to be distributed among the participants of the assembly at Freedom Square.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that in the early morning of 1 March 2008 the police tried to discover illegal items at Freedom Square and to prevent their use, for the purpose of verifying intelligence information regarding the illegal turnover of firearms, ammunition, explosive substances, explosive devices and various objects adapted to cause physical injuries for the purpose of instigating mass disorder in Yerevan.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and his co-thinkers were informed in advance about the police operation at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that as a result of the police operation on 1 March 2008, some objects brought for the purpose of mass disorder, including firearms and ammunition, were discovered at Freedom Square.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that after the police operation at Freedom Square, participants of the assembly, led by the applicant, S.S. and others, moved and gathered in the area adjacent to the Myasnikyan monument in Yerevan.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that at around 11 a.m. on 1 March 2008 the participants of the mass disorder blocked Grigor Lusavorich street by placing trolleybuses along the carriageway, after which they attacked the police officers upholding public order.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the participants of the mass disorder beat a number of police officers on several occasions.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the participants of the mass disorder armed themselves with objects including stones, rods and sticks, as well as explosive substances, explosive devices, firearms and Molotov cocktails which had been prepared beforehand and brought to the area of the mass disorder.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that Molotov cocktails were filled with flammable liquid immediately behind the platform at the Myasnikyan monument and in the nearby park.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and S.S., together with a group of others, arranged and managed the activities of other organisers and participants of the mass disorder.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that S.S., together with a group of others, regularly circulated among the participants of the mass disorder and organised their activities aimed at building barricades and showing armed resistance to the police.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that S.S., being in the epicentre of the mass disorder, regularly updated the applicant regarding the ongoing massacre, arson and the deliberate destruction, damage and looting of property, carrying out new orders received from the applicant.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the participants of the mass disorder beat a number of police officers on several occasions.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the participants of the mass disorder armed themselves with objects including stones, rods and sticks, as well as explosive substances, explosive devices, firearms and Molotov cocktails which had been prepared beforehand and brought to the area of the mass disorder.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that Molotov cocktails were filled with flammable liquid immediately behind the platform at the Myasnikyan monument and in the nearby park.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant and S.S., together with a group of others, arranged and managed the activities of other organisers and participants of the mass disorder.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that S.S., together with a group of others, regularly circulated among the participants of the mass disorder and organised their activities aimed at building barricades and showing armed resistance to the police.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that S.S., being in the epicentre of the mass disorder, regularly updated the applicant regarding the ongoing massacre, arson and the deliberate destruction, damage and looting of property, carrying out new orders received from the applicant.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan proceeded to describe the damage caused by the unrest in its judgment of 22 June 2009.

On 21 July 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal against the judgment of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan of 22 June 2009, raising numerous arguments including that the charge against him was trumped up and politically motivated.
On 31 July 2009 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the judgment of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan of 22 June 2009.
On 28 August 2009 the applicant lodged an appeal on points of law against the judgment of the Criminal Court of Appeal.
On 10 September 2009 the Court of Cassation declared the applicant's appeal on points of law inadmissible for lack of merit.

In its Resolutions regarding the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election and the events that followed, the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) condemned the arrest and continuing detention of scores of persons, including more than 100 opposition supporters and three members of parliament.

The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) condemned the arrest and continuing detention of persons on seemingly artificial and politically motivated charges, especially those under Articles 225 and 300 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The relevant extracts of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe (PACE) Resolutions and other relevant international materials regarding the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election and subsequent events are set out in Mushegh Saghatelyan v. Armenia (no. 23086/08, §§ 125-34, 20 September 2018) and Myasnik Malkhasyan v. Armenia (no. 49020/08, §§ 51-57, 15 October 2020).
